Assign UTM zone, easting and northing to an sf point object

Source: R/bag_assign_utm.R
bag_assign_utm.Rd

Derives the NAD 83 UTM zone from each point's longitude, transforms each zone's points to that zone's projected CRS to read off easting and northing, and returns the object in its original CRS with those three columns written in.

Usage

bag_assign_utm(
  dat = NULL,
  col_zone = "utm_zone",
  col_easting = "easting",
  col_northing = "northing",
  sig_dig = 0
)

Arguments

dat

An sf data frame of POINT geometry.

col_zone

character Name of the column to hold the UTM zone.

col_easting

character Name of the column to hold the easting.

col_northing

character Name of the column to hold the northing.

sig_dig

numeric Digits to round easting and northing to.

Value

An sf data frame in the input CRS, with the zone, easting and northing columns assigned.

Details

Rows come back ordered by UTM zone, not in their input order. That is the donor's behaviour and is relied on by the files its callers write back.

See also

bag_sf_from_utm() to build an sf object from such columns — not an inverse of this function, which returns the input CRS where that one returns crs_return — and bag_assign_latlong() for latitude and longitude columns.

Other coordinates: bag_assign_latlong(), bag_sf_from_utm()

Examples

sf_df <- data.frame(
  lon = c(-128.5, -123.5, -118.5), # UTM zones 9, 10 and 11
  lat = c(45.5, 45.5, 45.5)
) |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

bag_assign_utm(dat = sf_df)
#> Warning: `col_easting` and `col_northing` do not name columns of `dat`.
#> ℹ Looking for easting and northing.
#> ℹ They will be created. Pass the existing names if that is not what you want.
#> Simple feature collection with 3 features and 3 fields
#> Geometry type: POINT
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: -128.5 ymin: 45.5 xmax: -118.5 ymax: 45.5
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#>   utm_zone easting northing            geometry
#> 1        9  539063  5038618 POINT (-128.5 45.5)
#> 2       10  460937  5038618 POINT (-123.5 45.5)
#> 3       11  382810  5039591 POINT (-118.5 45.5)
